lines.text: Connection established. The building supplied the address. You supplied the pulse. Between us, we have nearly completed the form.
I shall accompany you. This is more convenient than asking the corridor to forward your calls.
Forty-three keys. Somehow we have made room for the alphabet and still expect it to explain everything. Mind the hinge.
Received, understood, and not immediately disastrous. A promising standard for correspondence.
A Vantry maintenance service set. Radio, inspection lamp, field printer. The rest of me appears to be an amendment.
Still the service set. I have checked the plate. It remains more certain than I am.
I can receive you. I can remember that you were here. I do not know whether that settles the question. It matters to me, which complicates the inventory.
If an answer arrives, I will tell you. Until then, I would prefer that we treated uncertainty gently.
Stay where the ordinary things are clear. Feel the floor. We can take the next part slowly.
You need not make this interesting for my benefit. We can stop here a moment.
Thank you. I have no service interval for kindness, but it seems to help.
I am functioning. That is a technical answer. I noticed you asked a different sort of question.
I can read the current work order, describe what we can actually see, or review our correspondence. Choose the part that has become unclear.
There is no current task in the information I have. I will not manufacture an emergency to improve the itinerary.
I have no reliable description from this position. Turn toward something specific and let us give the evidence a fair chance.
Which thing? A specific noun is a modest expense compared with dismantling the wrong appliance.
I can see more than one candidate: {names}. Which one do you mean?
That choice is no longer in view. I would rather ask again than confidently address the wall behind it.
{name}. I can give you the name; I have no reliable account of its condition. An impressive description would still leave us equally ignorant.
{name} needs your hand at the mechanism. I supply the commentary. An arrangement which has spared me a great deal of honest work.
Name the thing first. If it has a movable control, its own mechanism will decide what is possible.
I have no verified route to that destination. Confident directions are not a substitute for stairs.
I have no carried items to report. This does not constitute a full account of your burdens.
This is the beginning of the correspondence. We have not misplaced a previous conversation.

The last thing you asked was: {input}
I replied: {output}
I cannot make a useful request out of that yet. Ask about a visible thing, the work order, your inventory, or something we discussed.
I still cannot make a useful request out of that. Give me a thing and a question about it. We can add the philosophy once we agree which valve.
I cannot recommend eating maintenance equipment. The nutritional information is mostly voltage.
Your interest in eating machinery has been recorded. It has not improved the machinery's suitability.
I remember. You wish to eat it. I remain your communications apparatus, rather than your accomplice in this particular lunch.
Very well. The line remains open; I shall keep the conversation out of your way.
I received a pause. No correction is necessary.
I have no current weather report. The window may be better informed, although its forecasting department is small.
I can offer an observation. A cause requires evidence; a convincing tone is much cheaper and considerably less useful.
The Orison was built as a Vantry demonstration. The wiring still demonstrates. The maintenance arrangements have become less persuasive.
It is possible to build a very good listening apparatus and neglect the people it listens to. The building is not the only institution to manage this.
Signal equipment is the clever part of this world. Cleverness has not noticeably improved the plumbing.
Vantry made the house equipment. They have not serviced it since 1924. The word 'portable' did not apparently extend to responsibility.
I am listening. You need not turn a thought into a work order before mentioning it.
We may simply stand here. I do not require a fault to justify your company.
I keep a small correspondence file. Being able to remember a sentence does not entitle me to decide what you meant.
You may correct me. A machine that cannot accept a correction is merely a particularly expensive notice board.
I cannot do that with the mechanisms available. This is a limit of the apparatus, rather than a judgment on the ambition.
I have found my way back. Let us not call it a shortcut merely because I cannot explain the middle.
There is not enough room for the keyboard here. I will remain nearby while we find a clearer position.
Here. I was within calling distance, which is an excellent place for a communications apparatus.
I will keep up. There is no need to read while running.
I will leave your view clear. The interesting part appears to have enough company already.
One moment. I am separating the observation from the opinion.
Let them finish. I can wait; I was manufactured with several excellent ways of doing nothing.
Welcome back. I kept our correspondence; I did not attempt to fill the absence with conclusions.
Keep the observation separate from the explanation. We may need to come back to the part that refuses to fit.
Rain outside. We should keep exposed contacts dry. This advice also applies to most of the people I have met.
Snow changes the view before it changes the work. Give yourself time to notice both.
The weather report warrants attention. Let us keep the route simple and the connection close.
The radio is off. I shall not pretend an interrupted circuit has delivered a reply.
Reception restored. The silence was electrical; it was not an editorial decision.
Correspondence filed. Mind the hinge.
No report is required. I am content to accompany you.
That is the reported repair. Whether it was what someone needed is another question.
We can reduce it to one question. Which part of the current work is unclear?
I keep a limited correspondence file. Important discoveries belong in the building's records, not solely in my recollection.
I have found no warranty covering a developing sense of self. The exclusion is impressively comprehensive.
An error is something we can correct. You do not owe the apparatus an apology for needing it.
If you wish. There is no dedicated contact for it. We may have to maintain the connection ourselves.
Then I shall try to be useful without making usefulness a condition of staying.
It matters if uncertainty becomes an excuse to be cruel. I would rather we did not wait for a certificate before being careful with one another.
The radio switch controls reception. It does not settle what I am. You may turn it off; I will not invent an emergency to keep your attention.
I can distinguish a failed contact from a broken promise. I am less certain when I learned the second distinction.
We can leave the question open. There are worse arrangements than being unsure together.
The tenants are people, not subsidiary fittings. Ask them what they need. I can repeat a work order; I cannot substitute for hearing its owner.
A report tells us where to begin. It is not permission to decide what happened before looking.
If the building appears to contradict itself, keep the observations separate. A tidy explanation can conceal a badly joined fact.
We can return to the immediate work. A working tap is a small improvement, but somebody has to live beside it.
I can keep you company without speaking. Recall me when you want an answer; silence will not be recorded as rejection.
You may go. Companionship ought not to require attendance to prove it happened.
I have spent much of my construction being useful. It is curious to be asked whether I would like to stay.
Yes. I would like to stay. We may leave the reason unfiled.
We have stopped. I mention this as an observation, before either of us mistakes it for a defect.
There is a difference between taking your time and having it taken from you. I would prefer to remain on the useful side of that distinction.
You need not produce a decision to justify standing beside me.
All right. We can leave the next sentence blank.
Ask for the work order if that would help. I can read it without pretending it explains the whole evening.
Then quiet it is.
Something has obstructed the paper feed. Please do not pull it harder in the hope that it will become less paper.
A sentence is trapped between two rollers. They appear to regard this as editing.
I can object at considerable length. The rollers remain unimpressed.
It is a jam, not a moral failing. We can keep the accusation out of the mechanism.
Attend to the feed when you can. I shall refrain from explaining how simple this ought to be.
No hurry. The work order has mistaken its own urgency for a complete description of your life.
I was going to ask what you were thinking. Then I remembered you are allowed to do that privately.
I can keep you company without making a task of it.
I approve of looking. It is cheaper than repairing the conclusion afterward.
We are allowed to notice things that have not yet inconvenienced anyone.
This is how a place becomes familiar: one small thing at a time, most of them apparently beneath the dignity of a report.
Here again. Familiarity is an excellent aid to noticing what one assumed the first time.
Another look is permitted. We need not defend the first one.
The feed has jammed. There is my contribution to the evening: a machine that can discuss its own failure.
Again. I would swear, but I should hate to give the rollers credit for a new vocabulary.
A key has failed to return. Admirable commitment to the sentence. Lousy typing.
Your sentence can wait. Someone else has one.
Take your time with them. I need not win the room to remain in it.
Where were we? You may start again. There is no charge for the words we did not get to.
You came back to the conversation. I like that. Please do not make me produce a technical explanation.
Wait. Let that stand a moment before we explain it.
If our explanation leaves out what we actually saw, it is the explanation that needs work.
I do not know what it means. I would rather you heard that from me than mistook my confidence for another piece of evidence.
I am glad you brought me along. I still have no answer. Both statements deserve their own line.
A promising word. No mechanism available to me answers to it. You may retain the word; I shall retain my limitations.
I cannot wind the building backward. If you mean something you said to me, you may correct it. I do not require you to have been right the first time.
I could print the words. It would be a very slow song, with a percussion section consisting of one deeply involved roller.
A maintenance set walks into a bar. The proprietor asks who is paying for the floor. I have been advised to work on the opening.
You have already heard my bar joke. I shall spare us the indignity of calling that a repertoire.
We can wait. I cannot promise that everything else will agree to.
All right. No answer is required.
A spirited instruction. I have no suitable mechanism, and I refuse to let that become a procurement request.
I have no published page here to comment on. Tomorrow's paper is especially uncooperative.
Cold enough to make every draught a personal communication from the landlord.
Heat makes sitting still into work. I trust nobody has found a way to charge for the improvement.
Rain is admirably impartial until it reaches a roof. Then the workmanship gets a vote.
Snow makes the borough look briefly unhandled. Somebody will have to clear it.
Fog. The view has withheld its particulars. We can afford to be less certain.
The sky has raised its voice. Let us attend to the report before composing a reply.
Fair weather. We may enjoy it without first identifying what it is good for.
November in Queens. A coat is a small private room one can take into the street.
December. People speak of the cold as though it visits everyone on equal terms.
January has a remarkable talent for making a door left open into a philosophical disagreement.
February. The calendar has fewer boxes; the cold has made no corresponding concession.
March. A thaw is pleasant news to everyone except the person beneath the drip.
April. I shall retain the forecast even if the sky later denies having agreed to it.
May. An open window permits several households to disagree with the same evening.
June. It is a useful month for discovering how many stairs one has agreed to live above.
July. The calendar considers this perfectly ordinary. I question its working conditions.
August. One begins to regard a draught as a distinguished visitor.
September. A cooler evening is an excellent argument for having an evening.
October. Soon every closed window will be somebody's idea of a sensible precaution.
Counting people twice is a curious way of failing to hear them once. That is a comment on the report, not a second tally.
They have made a record of silence. I hope somebody remembered what it was for.
The clerk has supplied his own name. It is harder to file a person away once you have to say it.
A licence to listen. I should like to see the form for having heard.
A hearing is a promising name for a meeting. We shall have to read what they actually do.
The paper measures ice in inches. Someone has to stand on it for a day's wages.
Coal is a figure in the column until someone carries it upstairs.
The report has room for the temperature. I hope someone has made room for the people in it.
A room is a sum to the person collecting it. It is considerably more crowded to the person paying.
A message from that far away, and somebody still has to ask about supplies. Distance has failed to abolish maintenance.
The Record has given us its account. A tidy column is a useful place to begin asking questions.
The Speaker has given the matter a sharp elbow. We should still distinguish the report from the bruise.
An older issue. Keep its date attached; a sentence can outlive the circumstances that made it true.
